subject: Satisfactory absolute fit indices, but low CFI and TLI

messages.author: 9065d041a7201790
messages.subject: Satisfactory absolute fit indices, but low CFI and TLI
parts:
Dear all.

I'm trying to run a two-level CFA model, where a questionnaire of 52 items is loaded on 7 subscales, which are further loaded on 2 second-order factors. We have a sample of ~1200 participants. Whereas the RMSEA is 0.055, and the SRMR is 0.06, the CFI and TLI are ~0.83. Following the suggestion of Kenny (http://davidakenny.net/cm/fit.htm) I've tested the RMSEA of the null model which turned out to be 0.14 (which is smaller than 0.158, which Kenny suggests to indicate that "an incremental measure of fit may not be that informative"). I understand that this means that the correlations between items are not that high. I assume it has a lot to do with the fact the it is a highly multidimensional questionnaire, where some of the factors are indeed not so related (conceptually and statistically) to the other factors.
My question is - can this situation still count as a reasonable fit (and can it thus be published?). Also - does anyone knows of any academic papers discussing such a divergence between absolute and relative fit indices, and supporting Kenny's suggestion (which he only published in his website but not in an academic paper)?
Thanks!
Issac
